scope: DeepCrack | exploratory CPU study | measured results | separate from manuscript tables

figures.title: Learning curves
figures.caption: Training and validation BCE–Dice losses for all three matched runs. Curves cover the complete recorded training histories; augmentation affects training only. Checkpoint selection uses validation mIoU, not the minimum test loss. A widening train–validation gap would indicate overfitting; loss magnitude alone does not establish crack localization quality.

figures.title: Validation learning
figures.caption: Validation F1, two-class mIoU and the learning-rate schedule. Threshold 0.5 is fixed during model selection. Background-heavy mIoU can remain near 0.5 even when foreground F1 is zero. The learning rate halves after epoch 10; this setting is shared across models.

figures.title: Dataset composition
figures.caption: Image counts and source-group counts for the recorded train/validation/test split, together with distributions of original-resolution foreground fractions. The counts are computed from the analyzed manifest. Groups come from the recorded filename heuristic; differences between group and image proportions reflect correlated crops. The histogram shows why pixel accuracy must be interpreted alongside foreground F1.

figures.title: Measured segmentation results
figures.caption: Precision, recall, F1 and mIoU on the held-out test images; the right panel contrasts threshold 0.5 with thresholds selected using the validation images only. Whiskers show source-group bootstrap 95% percentile intervals for tuned test F1 (1,000 resamples). Swin + spatial achieved F1=0.592 and mIoU=0.694 at threshold 0.475. Intervals describe test-group sampling uncertainty conditional on one fitted model, not training-seed variation.

figures.title: Precision–recall curves
figures.caption: Test-set pixel precision–recall curves from 256 probability bins. Legend AP is explicitly the binned pixel AP approximation; it is not object mAP@0.5. The dashed line gives the test pixel foreground prevalence, a random-ranking reference. This descriptive test curve does not select the deployed threshold.

figures.title: Validation threshold selection
figures.caption: Validation precision, recall and F1 across the declared threshold grid (0.05–0.95, step 0.025). Each dashed vertical line marks the validation-F1 optimum, with deterministic tie handling. That value is frozen before test evaluation. Thresholds should be recalibrated on a validation population matching any new deployment domain.

figures.title: Confusion matrices
figures.caption: Pixel confusion matrices at the frozen validation-selected thresholds. Rows indicate true background/crack and columns predicted background/crack. Color is normalized within each true class; annotations retain raw pixel counts and row percentages. This makes missed cracks visible despite the much larger background class.

figures.title: Qualitative predictions
figures.caption: Three held-out Swin examples chosen by a declared rule: lowest, median and highest per-image test F1. Columns show resized RGB input, binary model input, ground truth, crack probability, predicted mask and an error map. Error colors: teal=true positive, orange=false positive, purple=false negative, white=true negative. Ranking is descriptive and intentionally includes a failure; the displayed images are not an unbiased random sample. Source imagery and annotations: Liu et al., DeepCrack (2019), under upstream terms.

figures.title: Photometric stress tests
figures.caption: Test F1 under deterministic brightness factors 0.6 and 1.4, Gaussian blur radius 1.2, and Gaussian RGB noise with standard deviation 0.05 on [0,1]. Perturbations occur before the trained grayscale/denoising/Otsu pipeline; labels and the selected threshold stay fixed. These are controlled sensitivity checks, not proof of real weather or cross-country robustness. Shared per-image random seeds make noise comparisons reproducible.

figures.title: Accuracy and efficiency
figures.caption: Single-device batch-one forward latency and model size at the same configured input resolution. The scatter relates measured test F1 to mean latency; the second panel reports trainable parameters. Timing uses 5 warmups, 30 measured iterations and 2 CPU threads, excluding image decoding, preprocessing and output writing. Architecture size and CPU throughput must not be compared directly with the manuscript RTX3090 full-model claims.
